long_biography.plain_text:
Anthony Bamford prepared for the family business through an engineering apprenticeship in France, then entered JCB on the shop floor. He moved into management through the company's early European export drive and took the chair when founder Joseph Cyril Bamford retired. His expansion programme combined overseas manufacturing with greater control over engines, transmissions and other major components.

Known formally as Lord Bamford, he remains JCB's chairman and continues to guide manufacturing and product development. Graeme Macdonald serves as chief executive, separating Bamford's strategic chairmanship from day-to-day executive management. JCB's factories and other operating assets belong to the privately owned company, while ownership of the business is held at the Bamford-family level rather than as Bamford's individual property.
